channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka (toe) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Bengals.
item.description: The Buccaneers had Egbuka take almost a month off to let the toe heal, which turned out to be a great call. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 wide receiver is good to go for Week 1. Nagging injuries slowed Egbuka’s rookie season. Entering 2026 in good health sets the stage for a bounce-back campaign. He is a WR2 with WR1 upside.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Kamara suffered an MCL injury during a scrimmage three weeks ago. The issue was initially expected to sideline him for at least a month, but it looks like he has a shot at significantly beating that timeline. Even if he doesn’t play this week, there’s a good chance Kamara is back by Week 2 or 3. He will be a low-end FLEX play in PPR leagues once he is healthy.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (heel) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description: The Bengals will have their top two wide receivers on the field for what should be a high-scoring game against the Buccaneers. Higgins is a high-end WR2 with WR1 upside, playing alongside WR1 Ja’Marr Chase this weekend.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description: Chase’s participation actually exceeds expectations. Beginning the week with a limited session would have been unsurprising. The Bengals’ star wide receiver hyperextended his knee on August 25th, but he is now good to go. Treat Chase as an elite WR1, per usual.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Branch ran behind Olamide Zaccheaus for most of training camp. A light workload in practice heading into Week 1 all but guarantees he won’t threaten the veteran receiver for a starting role to open the year. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar for his NFL debut versus the Steelers.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Giants TE Theo Johnson (shoulder) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Cowboys.
item.description: Johnson was seen practicing in a non-contact jersey last week, so today’s full session is positive. Unfortunately, Johnson’s path to fantasy football TE1 status is likely blocked by TE Isaiah Likely, so Johnson is not on the radar for most leagues.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cam Jordan (hamstring) will not play in Week 1 against the Lions.
item.description: Jordan has been dealing with a hamstring issue for nearly a month. The fact that Kellen Moore was able to rule him out so early in the week suggests this issue could linger for much longer than just Sunday’s game. Jordan signed a one-year deal with stay in New Orleans for a 16th season in June. He totaled 10.5 sacks in 2025.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description: Madubuike joined team drills last week, and is technically on track to play in Week 1 against the Colts. If active, the stud defensive tackle will likely be on a snap count, though the team could opt for a conservative approach and hold him out for this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Oscar Delp (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description: Delp has been out for multiple weeks with the hamstring issue. A DNP to open the season likely puts him on the wrong side of questionable. His absence will lock in Juwan Johnson as an every-down player, though that was barely a question even before this injury.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description: For the record, Flowers told reporters that he is feeling “great” earlier today, but opted not to disclose his injury details. Now we know he is dealing with a soft tissue issue. Flowers is on track to play, but as is always the case with hamstrings, his practice participation is worth tracking. Ideally, he is practicing fully by Friday and can be treated as a WR2 on game day.-Nic Bodiford
